summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic alcohol and substance use, was readmitted within hours of discharge due to reported syncope, ICD shocks, and hematemesis. He described two episodes of passing out with perceived defibrillator shocks and vomiting blood. Telemetry monitoring showed only a brief, asymptomatic run of ventricular tachycardia, and ICD interrogation confirmed no shocks were delivered. Labs, including serial hemoglobin, were stable, and imaging showed no acute intracranial or cardiopulmonary pathology. The GI team deferred endoscopy due to lack of objective bleeding. His symptoms were deemed inconsistent with device data and lab findings, raising concern for secondary gain. He was restarted on anticoagulation and discharged home with instructions to follow up with cardiology and primary care, continue PPI therapy, avoid alcohol, and monitor weight.
